# Preface {.unnumbered}

This companion follows the slides of **Chapter 5: Photodetectors and Image Sensors** (Basics of Optoelectronics, University of
Trento) section by section. The slides tell the story; this book lets you **compute it**. Every figure is made by a few lines of
Python that you can unfold ("Show the Python"), copy and modify. The **live panels** (marked with a blue bar on the left)
recompute directly in your browser. They need no installation.

## Where this chapter sits in the course

Chapter 1 described light as a wave, Chapter 2 guided it in fibers, Chapter 3 built the pn junction and the LED, and Chapter 4
the laser and the optical amplifier. Chapter 5 closes the link: the **photodetector** converts the optical power back into an
electrical current. It uses the same pn junction as the LED of Ch. 3, run in reverse: a photon of energy $h\nu>E_g$ creates an
electron–hole pair, the field of the depletion region separates it, and a current flows in the external circuit. Three questions
organise the chapter:

1. **How many electrons per photon?** Absorption coefficient, quantum efficiency, responsivity, and internal gain (avalanche
   photodiodes, photoconductors, phototransistors).
2. **How fast?** Drift and diffusion of the carriers (the Shockley–Ramo theorem), transit time, and the $RC$ constant of the
   junction capacitance and the load.
3. **How weak a signal?** Shot noise, thermal noise, excess avalanche noise, SNR, NEP and detectivity, which set the
   sensitivity of every fiber receiver (Ch. 2) and the noise floor that the EDFA of Ch. 4 must beat.

The same physics then makes **image sensors** (CCD and CMOS arrays of photodiodes) and, in forward bias with a load, **solar cells**.

A **formula sheet** is at the end.

::: {.callout-note}
## Units in the code
The code works in **SI units** (m, m⁻¹, A, W, F). Absorption coefficients are in m⁻¹, as on the slides. The avalanche section of
the slides quotes ionisation coefficients in cm⁻¹ and fields in V cm⁻¹; the APD functions use those units and say so.
Photon and band energies are in **eV**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Slide numbers
Slide numbers refer to `chapter5_ Photodetectors.ppt` (152 slides).
:::

## Using the code

All functions live in a small, readable module, [`detlib.py`](detlib.py), which you can import from your own notebooks:

```python
import detlib as dl
dl.responsivity(0.6, 1.55e-6)                  # A/W of a 60 % QE detector at 1550 nm
dl.snr(Iph=5e-9, Id=2e-9, B=1e6, RL=1e4)       # SNR of the receiver of slide 104
```

See the appendix [Running the notebooks](running.qmd) for installation.
